title: Permissions Tree
statement: Build a nested permissions picker. Ticking a folder grants everything under it and unticking it takes it all away, while a folder with only some of its children granted has to show as partially selected rather than on or off. The line underneath lists exactly what is granted right now, and the tree nests as deep as the data does.

rubric: State is held for the leaves only; a folder's checked and indeterminate state is derived from what is under it, never stored alongside it.
The tree is built recursively from the data, so a deeper node needs no new code.
Ticking a folder grants every leaf beneath it, including through an intermediate folder.
A folder with some but not all of its leaves granted renders as indeterminate, and the CSS makes that visibly different from both other states.
The summary line is recomputed from the same state the tree is drawn from, so the two cannot disagree.
curveballs: Actually, make the summary show a count per top-level group instead of the full list.
Add a collapse arrow so a folder can be folded away without losing its state.
Grey out the billing permission entirely and make it ungrantable.
